overview: This file consists of an April 17, 1947 letter from the Standard-Vacuum Oil Company concerning a proposal for private oil companies to bunker American and other foreign-flag commercial vessels at Yokohama during the Allied occupation of Japan. The company describes anticipated monthly demand, payment in U.S. dollars or sterling, the potential benefit to the Occupation Forces, and a proposed investigation of its petroleum-storage and fueling facilities at Tsurumi.

people.name: Edwin M. Martin
people.role: Chief, Division of Japanese & Korean Economic Affairs, U.S. Department of State

people.name: D. Draper
people.role: Standard-Vacuum Oil Company representative and signatory

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum proposal for bunkering foreign vessels at Yokohama
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese & Korean Economic Affairs, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: The letter proposes that private oil companies assume responsibility for bunkering American and other foreign-flag commercial vessels at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Draper reports that the ANPB would be agreeable to transferring the bunkering of American and other foreign-flag vessels in Japan to oil companies, with estimated demand of 60,000–100,000 barrels per month. Because payment would be made in U.S. dollars or sterling, no yen exchange rate would be required, and the arrangement might reduce the burden on the Occupation Forces. Subject to government approval, Standard-Vacuum seeks authorization for an employee in Japan to examine whether its Tsurumi installation and its available storage tanks could support the proposed service.

interest: The letter provides a compact illustration of how commercial petroleum companies sought to resume or expand operations under the Allied occupation of Japan. It is particularly useful for its quantitative estimate of bunker-fuel demand, its discussion of dollar and sterling payments outside the yen exchange system, and its evidence concerning the surviving storage capacity at Standard-Vacuum's Tsurumi terminal. It also documents the proposed transfer of a logistical function from occupation authorities to private enterprise.
